meta.author: Logicanvas.io
notes: Elementor is optional. Core auctions work with shortcodes and theme templates.
WooCommerce is required. Payments always go through WooCommerce gateways.
Do not install alongside the branded auction-platform plugin; both use the wcap_ table prefix.
Setup is a single Create auction pages action (not a multi-step wizard). Existing mapped pages are skipped.

faq.question: What is Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce?
faq.answer: Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce is a WooCommerce plugin for timed and live auctions. Store owners and approved third-party holders can list lots. Registered bidders place bids on the server. Winners pay through normal WooCommerce checkout, tax, shipping, and payment gateways.

faq.question: Is WooCommerce required?
faq.answer: Yes. WooCommerce must be installed and active. The plugin shows an admin notice and fails gracefully if WooCommerce is missing. It never stores card numbers and never bypasses your store’s payment gateways.

faq.question: Is Elementor required?
faq.answer: No. Elementor is optional. Shortcodes, templates, REST endpoints, and dashboards work without Elementor. If Elementor is active, dedicated widgets and dynamic tags become available.

faq.question: What versions are supported?
faq.answer: WordPress 6.4 or newer, PHP 8.1 or newer, and WooCommerce 8.0 or newer. HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) and block checkout compatibility are declared.

faq.question: What is the difference between timed and live auctions?
faq.answer: A timed auction runs for a fixed start and end window. Bidders place bids until the auction closes automatically (with optional soft-close extensions). A live auction uses a lobby and live room controlled by the holder: open lobby, start, pause/resume, going once/twice, extend, sell, mark unsold, or cancel. In both modes the server—not the browser—is authoritative for price, winner, and state.

faq.question: Who can create auctions?
faq.answer: Site administrators can create and manage auctions. Third-party users must apply to become an auction holder, be approved by an administrator, and then create or submit auctions from the holder dashboard. Suspended holders cannot publish or host.

faq.question: How do I become an auction holder?
faq.answer: Open the Become an auction holder page (created by Setup, shortcode [wcap_holder_apply]), submit the application, and wait for administrator approval. Statuses are pending, approved, rejected, or suspended.

faq.question: Who can place a bid?
faq.answer: Authenticated users with bidding capability can bid on auctions they are allowed to access. Guests can usually view public auctions but must log in (or register) before bidding. Nobody may bid on their own auction, including administrators acting as holders.

faq.question: Can I bid on my own auction?
faq.answer: No. Self-bidding is always rejected by the server, even if the user has both holder and bidder capabilities.

faq.question: How are bids accepted?
faq.answer: Every bid is validated on the server: auction state, time window, eligibility, currency, minimum increment, rate limits, and idempotency. The auction row is locked during acceptance. Duplicate clicks with the same idempotency key return the original result instead of creating another bid. The first valid committed bid wins a tie.

faq.question: What is soft close (anti-sniping)?
faq.answer: On timed auctions, if a valid bid arrives within the last soft-close window (default 120 seconds), the end time is extended (default +120 seconds), up to a maximum number of extensions (default 20). The new end time is stored and broadcast from the server.

faq.question: What happens if the reserve is not met?
faq.answer: If the auction ends below the reserve price, it can close as reserve not met / unsold according to the state machine. Public displays typically show only whether the reserve is met, not the hidden reserve amount (configurable reserve display policy).

faq.question: Is proxy (maximum) bidding available?
faq.answer: Proxy / maximum bidding for timed auctions exists as a strategy but is off by default in settings. It is not enabled for live auctions by default. Maximum values stay private.

faq.question: What visibility options exist?
faq.answer: Public (listed), unlisted (share link, not in public listings), and private/invite-only (invitation required). Invitation tokens are stored as hashes, can expire or be revoked, and never replace authentication for bidding.

faq.question: How does the winner pay?
faq.answer: When an auction closes with a winner, an award record is created with the final amount and a payment deadline (default 48 hours). Only that winner can start checkout. Quantity is locked to one and the line price is the awarded amount. Taxes and shipping use WooCommerce. Coupons and mixed carts can be disallowed in settings.

faq.question: What if the winner does not pay?
faq.answer: After the payment deadline, the award can be marked defaulted. The plugin does not automatically charge bidders. It does not automatically offer the lot to a runner-up unless that policy is explicitly enabled.

faq.question: How do commissions and seller payouts work?
faq.answer: The website is the checkout merchant. Each auction records its holder. Settlements track gross amount, commission, fees, refunds, net amount, and payout status. V1 supports manual payout tracking (pending, approved, paid, reversed, disputed). There is no automatic marketplace payout (for example Stripe Connect) in this edition; a payout provider interface exists for later integrations. Holders can request payouts and upload proof where the UI allows; administrators manage settlement status.

faq.question: What currency is used?
faq.answer: Each auction is locked to the store currency at creation. If the store currency changes later, mixed-currency settlement should be blocked until handled explicitly. Multi-currency auction settlement needs a dedicated integration.

faq.question: How do I create the frontend pages?
faq.answer: In wp-admin open Auctions → Setup and click Create auction pages. The wizard creates ordinary WordPress pages with shortcodes. You can edit them in the block editor or Elementor. Deleted pages are not recreated automatically unless you run setup again for missing keys.

faq.question: Which shortcodes are available?
faq.answer: wcap_auction_grid, wcap_single_auction, wcap_live_room, wcap_live_host, wcap_submit_auction, wcap_holder_dashboard, wcap_bidder_dashboard, wcap_my_bids, wcap_my_wins, wcap_pay_award, wcap_holder_apply, wcap_login, wcap_register, wcap_countdown, wcap_bid_panel, wcap_bid_history. See the shortcodes section in guided docs for attributes.

faq.question: How do live rooms stay in sync?
faq.answer: The default realtime mode is authenticated REST polling by event sequence (about 1 second while live, slower in lobby/paused). Push providers can notify clients that new state exists, but clients must still load authoritative state from WordPress. A push message cannot accept a bid or declare a winner.

faq.question: Auctions did not close on time. Why?
faq.answer: Closing uses WooCommerce Action Scheduler (WP-Cron fallback). If cron is delayed, opening an auction page or state endpoint after end time still runs an idempotent close. Check WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions and hosting cron reliability.

faq.question: Does uninstall delete my data?
faq.answer: Deactivation never deletes business data. Uninstall deletes tables and auction posts only if Remove all plugin data on uninstall is enabled in settings (default is off).

faq.question: How is personal data handled?
faq.answer: The plugin integrates with WordPress personal data export and erase tools. Financial/transaction rows may be anonymized rather than deleted when retention requires them. Public bidder identities are masked/aliased. IP addresses can be hashed. Terms acceptance can record timestamp and terms version.

faq.question: Can I override templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Copy templates into your-theme/logicanvas-auctions/ using the same relative paths as the plugin templates/ folder.

faq.question: Can I run this with another auction-platform plugin?
faq.answer: Do not activate this edition on a site that already runs the branded auction-platform plugin. They share the wcap_ table prefix and must not be installed together.

faq.question: Does the plugin store credit card details?
faq.answer: No. Payments are processed only through configured WooCommerce gateways. The plugin never collects or stores raw card details.

faq.question: Where do I manage auctions in wp-admin?
faq.answer: Under the Auctions menu (wcap-dashboard): Dashboard, Add Auction, All Auctions, Holders, Bids, Awards, Settlements, Settings, Diagnostics, and Setup Wizard. Exact items depend on capabilities.

faq.question: Is there a dedicated login page?
faq.answer: Yes. Setup creates a Log in page with [wcap_login] for login, register, lost password, and reset flows. Settings can redirect users to holder/bidder dashboards after login and optionally restrict wp-admin for those roles.

faq.question: Which emails are sent?
faq.answer: Notifications cover approval/rejection, scheduling, live start, bid accepted, outbid, reserve met (without revealing hidden reserve), extensions, winner, unsuccessful bidders, payment reminders, deadline expiry, payment received, holder sale, settlement updates, and cancellations. Users may manage preferences where offered. Noisy live-session emails can be throttled.

faq.question: Is there a REST API?
faq.answer: Yes. Namespace logicanvas-auctions/v1. Cookie authentication plus a REST nonce is required for write routes. Public GET responses hide private fields such as emails, IPs, and proxy maxima.

faq.question: Are WP-CLI commands available?
faq.answer: Yes: wp logicanvas-auctions list, close, overdue, rebuild, schema, diagnostics, reschedule, migrate.

faq.question: When does an auction accept bids?
faq.answer: Timed auctions accept bids only while active. Live auctions accept bids while live, going once, or going twice. A bid during going once/twice can reset the live state back to live. Lobby and paused states do not accept bidding.

guides.title: Install and activate Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce

steps.title: Install WooCommerce
steps.body: Install and activate WooCommerce. Configure store currency, tax, shipping, and at least one payment gateway.

steps.title: Install Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce
steps.body: Upload the logicanvas-auctions plugin ZIP or copy the logicanvas-auctions folder into wp-content/plugins/.

steps.title: Activate the plugin
steps.body: Activate Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce. Confirm there is no conflicting auction-platform plugin active.

steps.title: Run Setup
steps.body: Go to Auctions → Setup and create the frontend pages.

steps.title: Verify scheduler
steps.body: Confirm Action Scheduler / WP-Cron is healthy under WooCommerce → Status → Scheduled Actions so auctions close and payment reminders run on time.

steps.title: Open the wizard
steps.body: In wp-admin open Auctions → Setup.

steps.title: Create pages
steps.body: Click Create auction pages. This is a single action (not multi-step). The wizard creates ordinary WordPress pages and stores their IDs in the wcap_pages option. Existing mapped page IDs that still exist are skipped.

steps.title: Review assigned pages
steps.body: Confirm keys are assigned: archive, single, live, submit, holder, bidder, my_bids, my_wins, pay, terms, apply, login.

steps.title: Edit page content
steps.body: Edit any page in the block editor or Elementor. Keep the shortcode (or widget) that powers the feature. Customize surrounding layout as needed.

steps.title: Publish auction terms
steps.body: Replace the placeholder on the Auction terms page with your legal terms. Terms version is tracked in settings (terms_version).

steps.title: Open settings
steps.body: Go to Auctions → Settings.

steps.title: Set bidding defaults
steps.body: Configure default minimum increment, soft-close window, soft-close extension length, and max extensions.

steps.title: Set payment deadline
steps.body: Choose payment_deadline_hours (default 48) so winners know how long they have to pay.

steps.title: Configure commission
steps.body: Set commission_fixed, commission_percent, and commission_minimum used when calculating holder settlements.

steps.title: Checkout rules
steps.body: Decide whether coupons are allowed on auction checkout and whether auction wins may mix with normal cart items.

steps.title: Account and privacy options
steps.body: Optionally redirect logins to dashboards, restrict wp-admin for holders/bidders, hash IP addresses, and control uninstall data removal.

steps.title: Know the domain roles
steps.body: The plugin adds wcap_auction_holder and wcap_auction_bidder. Administrators receive all plugin capabilities.

steps.title: Authorize by capability
steps.body: Permission checks use capabilities (not hard-coded role names).

steps.title: Remember self-bid ban
steps.body: Holders also receive bidder capabilities but still cannot bid on their own auctions.

steps.title: Applicant submits form
steps.body: The user opens Become an auction holder and submits [wcap_holder_apply].

steps.title: Review in admin
steps.body: Open Auctions → Holders (or holder applications screen) and review the pending account.

steps.title: Approve, reject, or suspend
steps.body: Approve to allow creating/hosting. Reject or later suspend to block publishing and hosting.

steps.title: Confirm notification
steps.body: The holder should receive an approval or rejection notification when email is configured.

guides.title: Create and run a timed auction (administrator)

steps.title: Create the auction
steps.body: Create a timed auction from admin or the submission UI. Link or create a WooCommerce product, set title, description, gallery, starting price, optional reserve, increment, start/end times, visibility, and terms.

steps.title: Moderate if needed
steps.body: If workflow requires review, approve the auction so it can schedule or go active.

steps.title: Publish schedule
steps.body: Ensure start and end times are correct in store timezone understanding; server stores UTC canonically.

steps.title: Monitor bidding
steps.body: Watch bid audit screens as needed. Soft close may extend the end time near close.

steps.title: Closing and award
steps.body: At end, the server determines winner, reserve result, award, and payment deadline. Confirm Action Scheduler jobs if close seems delayed.

steps.title: Payment and completion
steps.body: When the winner pays via WooCommerce, order events update auction, award, and settlement state.

steps.title: Create a live auction
steps.body: Create a live-type auction with product details, starting price, increment, and visibility. Submit for review if required.

steps.title: Share the room URL
steps.body: Share the live room page URL (shortcode [wcap_live_room id="AUCTION_ID"] or assigned live page with auction context).

steps.title: Open the lobby
steps.body: From the host console ([wcap_live_host id="AUCTION_ID"]), open the lobby so participants can join before bidding starts.

steps.title: Start the auction
steps.body: Start live bidding. Participants see current price, increment controls, and server-synced status.

steps.title: Control the room
steps.body: Pause/resume, adjust increment when permitted, mark going once / going twice, extend time, sell to current leader, mark unsold, or cancel with a reason.

steps.title: Settle the sale
steps.body: After sold/payment pending, the winner pays through WooCommerce like a timed auction award.

guides.title: Create an auction as a holder

steps.title: Open submit or holder dashboard
steps.body: Use [wcap_submit_auction] or the holder dashboard create view.

steps.title: Fill listing details
steps.body: Add title, descriptions, images, condition, prices, schedule, fulfilment type, and terms acknowledgement.

steps.title: Save draft or submit
steps.body: Edit own drafts, then submit for review when ready.

steps.title: Wait for approval
steps.body: After approval, the auction schedules or becomes available according to type and start time.

steps.title: Track results
steps.body: Use listings, orders, and payouts views in the holder dashboard.

steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.body: Visit the Auction holder dashboard page ([wcap_holder_dashboard]).

steps.title: Review metrics
steps.body: Check overview metrics for upcoming, live, sold, and unsettled items.

steps.title: Manage listings
steps.body: Use listings to find drafts, pending review, live, and completed auctions.

steps.title: Manage orders and payouts
steps.body: Open orders for WooCommerce-linked sales and payouts for settlement requests / status.

guides.title: Register or log in to bid

steps.title: Open the login page
steps.body: Go to the Log in page created by Setup ([wcap_login]).

steps.title: Register or sign in
steps.body: Create an account if registration is enabled, or sign in with existing credentials.

steps.title: Land on dashboard
steps.body: If login redirect is enabled, you are sent to the appropriate bidder or holder dashboard.

steps.title: Browse auctions
steps.body: Open the Auctions archive ([wcap_auction_grid]) and choose a lot.

steps.title: Read terms and details
steps.body: Review description, condition, shipping/pickup, current price, next minimum bid, and countdown.

steps.title: Accept terms if required
steps.body: If require_terms is enabled, acknowledge auction terms before bidding.

steps.title: Submit a bid
steps.body: Use quick bid (next increment) or enter a custom amount, then confirm. Wait for server confirmation.

steps.title: Watch leading / outbid state
steps.body: Track status on the auction page, My bids, or bidder dashboard. You may receive outbid emails.

steps.title: Open bidder dashboard
steps.body: Visit [wcap_bidder_dashboard] or My bids / My wins pages.

steps.title: Track activity
steps.body: Review active bids, leading, outbid, watchlist, wins, and payment-required awards.

steps.title: Manage preferences
steps.body: Update notification preferences and account/address details where available.

steps.title: Open payment action
steps.body: Use the winner notification, My wins, or Pay for won auction page ([wcap_pay_award]).

steps.title: Confirm you are the winner
steps.body: Only the awarded user can start checkout. Ownership is revalidated on every request.

steps.title: Complete WooCommerce checkout
steps.body: Quantity and price are locked to the award. Choose shipping/pickup as offered and pay with a configured gateway.

steps.title: Keep the deadline
steps.body: Pay before the payment deadline. After expiry the award may default.

guides.title: Manage commissions and payouts
prerequisites: At least one paid auction order

steps.title: Open settlements
steps.body: Go to Auctions → Settlements.

steps.title: Review ledger fields
steps.body: Check gross amount, commission, fees, refunds, net amount, and payout status for each settlement.

steps.title: Handle holder payout requests
steps.body: Review pending payout requests and any uploaded transaction proof. Mark statuses such as approved, paid, reversed, or disputed according to your process.

steps.title: Keep refunds in sync
steps.body: When WooCommerce refunds or cancels orders, confirm settlement rows update. Do not pay holders for reversed amounts.

steps.title: Add a shortcode to a page
steps.body: Edit any WordPress page and paste a shortcode into the content, or use an Elementor shortcode/widget equivalent.

steps.title: Pass attributes where supported
steps.body: Use documented attributes such as id, type, state, and per_page.

steps.title: Combine modular pieces
steps.body: On custom layouts you can combine [wcap_countdown], [wcap_bid_panel], and [wcap_bid_history] with a known auction id.

attributes.id: auction id; falls back to current CPT or ?auction_id=

shortcodes.purpose: Bid form panel (renders the single-auction bidding UI for an id)
shortcodes.notes: Alias-style mount around the bidding experience for modular layouts.

shortcodes.purpose: Registration view helper (same auth UI as login register view)

steps.title: Confirm Elementor is optional
steps.body: If Elementor is inactive, keep using shortcodes. Do not require Elementor for core auctions.

steps.title: Edit a Setup page in Elementor
steps.body: Open any assigned auction page and edit with Elementor.

steps.title: Insert Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce widgets
steps.body: Use modular widgets: Auction Grid, Search/Filters, Single Auction, Gallery, Details, Current Price, Countdown, Bid Panel, Bid History, Live Room, Host Console, dashboards, submission, status, share, login.

steps.title: Use dynamic tags carefully
steps.body: When available, dynamic tags can output auction ID, prices, end time, countdown, state, type, bid count, reserve-met, holder name, and condition. Never expose privileged data in editor previews.

steps.title: Style responsively
steps.body: Configure typography, colors, spacing, and empty states per widget. Keep bidding controls keyboard accessible.

guides.title: Use public, unlisted, and invite-only auctions

steps.title: Choose visibility
steps.body: Select public for catalog listing, unlisted for share-link access without public listing, or private/invite-only for invited users.

steps.title: Distribute access safely
steps.body: Share unlisted links carefully. For invites, generate tokens that can expire, revoke, or bind to email/user.

steps.title: Require login to bid
steps.body: Viewing may be public, but bidding always requires an authenticated eligible bidder.

steps.title: WooCommerce missing notice
steps.body: Activate WooCommerce. Logicanvas Auctions for WooCommerce cannot process winners without it.

steps.title: Elementor widgets missing
steps.body: Expected when Elementor is inactive. Use shortcodes instead.

steps.title: Auction did not close
steps.body: Check Action Scheduler. Open the auction page after end time to trigger idempotent close failsafe. Use WP-CLI: wp logicanvas-auctions overdue or wp logicanvas-auctions close <id>.

steps.title: Bids rejected
steps.body: Confirm login, eligibility, not self-bidding, correct increment, auction accepting bids, and rate limits not exceeded.

steps.title: Winner cannot pay
steps.body: Confirm award ownership, deadline not expired, gateway configured, and coupons/mixed-cart settings not blocking unexpectedly.

steps.title: Live room stale
steps.body: Confirm realtime_mode polling, browser tab visibility, REST nonce/session valid, and clients recover from last sequence.

steps.title: Run diagnostics
steps.body: Use Auctions → Diagnostics or wp logicanvas-auctions diagnostics / schema.

guides.title: Privacy and security essentials

steps.title: Keep payments in WooCommerce
steps.body: Never collect cards outside WooCommerce gateways.

steps.title: Use Tools → Export/Erase personal data
steps.body: Plugin hooks support WordPress privacy tools; financial rows may be anonymized.

steps.title: Review public bid display
steps.body: Public names are aliased/filtered. Do not expose emails or IPs in public templates.

steps.title: Control uninstall data
steps.body: Leave remove_data_on_uninstall false unless you intentionally want tables deleted on uninstall.

security_highlights: Capability + ownership checks on REST and forms
Nonces for CSRF; capabilities for authorization
Rate limits on bidding, auth, applications, uploads
No eval / unsafe unserialize / raw card storage

steps.title: Use the namespace
steps.body: All routes live under /wp-json/logicanvas-auctions/v1/.

steps.title: Authenticate writes
steps.body: Send cookie auth plus a valid REST nonce for POST routes.

steps.title: Poll events by sequence
steps.body: Live clients call GET /auctions/{id}/events incrementally. Recover from last confirmed sequence after reconnect.

steps.title: Never trust push alone
steps.body: If a push transport is configured, treat it as a wake signal only. Authoritative state always comes from WordPress.

steps.title: Locate plugin templates
steps.body: Copy files from wp-content/plugins/logicanvas-auctions/templates/.

steps.title: Place overrides
steps.body: Put them in your-theme/logicanvas-auctions/ with the same relative path.

steps.title: Keep escaping and i18n
steps.body: Preserve escaping, text domain logicanvas-auctions, and do not move business rules into templates.

glossaries.definition: Approved seller who can create and host auctions.
Registered user who can place bids on eligible auctions.
Immutable record linking winner, final amount, currency, and payment deadline after a successful close.
Ledger row for gross sale, commission, fees, refunds, net amount, and payout status.
Anti-sniping extension of a timed auction end time when late bids arrive.
Monotonic auction event/version number used for realtime polling and cache invalidation.
Client-generated key that makes repeated bid requests return the original result.
